rationale: PINS THE THIRD EXPLANATION DIMENSION. The lane already enforces two and states both: `confidence < 1.0 => metadata.reasonCode` and `target is a reference (not contains/renders) => metadata.bindReason`, each measured at 100% on go-tools + terraform (312,620 of 312,620 and 332,160 of 332,160). What was silently incomplete is `metadata.relationshipType`, the construct that produced the edge — the key the sub-1.0 reason table READS (`GO_SUB_UNIT_REASON[type|relationshipType]`) and the key a consumer groups by to tell constructs apart. TEN of the twelve firing types carried it; `imports` and `contains` carried none, and `contains` shipped a literal BARE `metadata: {}`. MEASURED on that population: 55,012 of 363,830 edges (15.1%) named no construct, and `imports` was reaching its reason code only through the `imports|*` WILDCARD — correct by fallback rather than by name. After the fix all three dimensions are 100%: reasonCode 312,620/312,620, bindReason 332,160/332,160, construct label 363,830/363,830. THE THREE CONTAINS ROWS ARE THE REASON THIS IS A LABEL AND NOT A CONSTANT: this pass is the one place that knows WHICH ownership relation it is emitting, so the label is read off the member rather than guessed — a struct field, a method on its receiver type, and an interface method are three DIFFERENT Go relations that `contains` used to flatten into one unlabelled shape. Pinning all three distinct labels is what makes the row informative; a single `contains`-level label would satisfy presence while saying nothing. THE IMPORTS ROW pins the second half: it must carry BOTH its construct AND its reason code, because `imports` is sub-1.0 (0.9) and the reason table must now reach its code BY NAME rather than through the wildcard. NOT PINNED: confidence values and evidenceClass, which `classifyEvidenceTier` derives from confidence and which no row here changes; and the `exports`/`references` rows, which already carried their labels and are controls the other fixtures own.

expectRelationships.comment: OWNERSHIP RELATION 1: a struct field. Before the fix this edge carried a BARE metadata object and no construct at all.
OWNERSHIP RELATION 2: a method on its receiver type — a different Go relation from a field, and the label must say so.
OWNERSHIP RELATION 3: an interface method. Three distinct relations, three distinct labels — a single flat `contains` label would pass a presence check while telling a consumer nothing.

The second type that published no label. An import is sub-1.0 (0.9), so this row must carry BOTH the construct AND the reason code — the table must reach `imports` by NAME now, not through its `imports|*` wildcard.
CONTROL: a type that already carried its label keeps it, so the fix is additive and cannot have been achieved by relabelling everything to one value.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE DEFECT ITSELF: a `contains` edge with NO construct label is the bare-metadata shape this fixture exists to keep out. Scoped by meta.relationshipType: null so it forbids the ABSENCE rather than any particular value.
The same absence on the imports surface — the second of the two types that used to publish no construct.
